data.narrative:
Senra Systems is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $112M+ to date. The valuation analysis triangulates across a peer set of 3 private companies at the same stage and sector (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, and Dexterity at $1.6B), alongside 1 public comparable, forming part of a broader 9-company private frontier-tech robotics universe.

Two methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $112M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding $213M. Peer-median analysis across the 3 same-stage, same-sector private comparables produces a median valuation of $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B to $2.0B. These represent substantially different signals, reflecting both the heterogeneity within Series B robotics valuations and Senra's position relative to better-capitalized peers.

The triangulated range spans $181M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $981M. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around Senra's relative competitive positioning, unit economics maturity, and technology differentiation relative to the peer cohort. Key uncertainties include deployment traction, gross margins at scale, and whether Senra's capabilities justify valuation toward the higher peer quartile ($1.8B–$2.0B) or whether a discount to median peers is warranted given the stage-progression method's more conservative $213M signal.
